q: AI labs paying for human data 2026 Mercor Surge Scale
found: Mercor reportedly passed a 2 billion dollar yearly run rate selling expert human data to AI labs.
thought: Experts judging and doing real tasks is what sells; look for an open spot ordinary people could fill for free.

q: game where users try to stump AI with hard questions, sold to AI labs
found: Only research papers (Dynabench 2021, Trick Me If You Can); no consumer game that sells the data showed up.
thought: Check if Dynabench or Humanity Last Exam style crowd efforts still run and are free.

q: Humanity Last Exam crowdsourced questions prize; Dynabench status
found: HLE was built by paid experts with a prize pool; ordinary people rarely can write questions that beat top AI.
thought: Stump-the-AI game needs experts, so it is weak for ordinary users; dropping it and looking at consumer apps that already sell data to AI labs.

found: Needs expert-level questions; ordinary users cannot stump frontier models, and Dynabench/HLE already cover it.

q: consumer apps paying users for data sold to AI labs (Neon, Kled, Silencio)
found: Several gig apps pay users for call, video and sound data and Neon raised 25 million dollars, so buyers exist but they pay users rather than offer a free tool.
thought: Open spot: a free tool people want, data as by-product. Voice with accents looks promising: test how well AI hears you, share the score.

q: free accent test / does AI understand your accent
found: Free accent-guessing tools exist (Fluently, DEV accent detector) and a business tester (Cekura); none found that shows how speech AIs mishear YOU and collects fixes.
thought: Gap is close but accent guessers are the nearest rivals; now check who buys accented speech data and at what price.

q: who buys accented English speech data, price
found: Defined.ai, Nexdata and David AI sell accented speech datasets, with a self-serve data plan and a datarade listing, so a public market exists.
thought: Check David AI size to see if investors fund this kind of data.

q: David AI speech data startup funding
found: Bloomberg: David AI raised 50 million dollars at a 500 million valuation for audio data for AI models (Oct 2025).
thought: Investors do fund this. Now find the closest free rivals: BoldVoice accent oracle and Common Voice.

q: BoldVoice Accent Oracle; Common Voice accents; voice AI accent testing
found: BoldVoice Accent Oracle is a free speak-and-we-guess-your-accent tool already live; Common Voice is free open data; accent testing for voice AI exists for businesses.
thought: Oracle is the closest rival and also proof people share accent tools; open its page for traffic and data-use facts.

found: 189 upvotes, a commenter said it was going viral, no word on how voice samples are used; it upsells a paid app.
thought: Proves accent games spread and is the closest rival; my twist is showing what speech AIs typed for you and collecting fixes, for AI builders.

q: speech recognition fails accents word error rate studies
found: Several papers and a VentureBeat story show top speech AIs make more errors for some accents, so the pain is real and documented.
thought: Good hook for a share card: how much did the AI mishear you.

q: Speech Accent Archive and tools comparing speech AIs on your voice
found: Speech Accent Archive is a small free university collection of one fixed paragraph; no consumer tool found that shows several speech AIs side by side on your voice.
thought: Open spot looks real but narrow; write up with BoldVoice as the main rival and the cost and law risks.
